# Copilot Instructions

## Commands

- Install dependencies: `uv sync`
- Prepare local model settings: `cp .env.template .env`, then set `MODEL_NAME`, `API_BASE`, and `API_KEY`
- Run the agent against a description file: `uv run main.py path/to/description.md`
- Run the included sample: `uv run main.py samples/mixed-conversation.md`
- Override model settings from the CLI: `uv run main.py -m <model-id> -b <api-base> -k <api-key> path/to/description.md`
- Run tests: `uv run -m pytest`

## High-level architecture

- `main.py` is the CLI entrypoint. It loads `.env`, lets CLI flags override environment variables, reads a domain-description file from disk, and passes the formatted task prompt into `ModelAgent`.
- `agent.py` creates one shared `EPackage` root model and exposes generated domain tools to a `smolagents.CodeAgent`. The agent is intentionally restricted to those tools with `add_base_tools=False`.
- `prompts.py` contains the single task prompt template. It explains the supported Ecore subset to the LLM and injects the user description inside `<description>...</description>`.
- `model_types.py` defines the intermediate metamodel representation with Pydantic models: `EPackage`, `EClass`, `EAttribute`, `EReference`, and `EDataType`.
- `model_tools.py` is the generated tool layer used by `smolagents`. Each tool mutates the shared Pydantic object graph in place so the final metamodel is assembled incrementally across tool calls.

## Key conventions

- `model_tools.py`, `model_types.py`, and `prompts.py` are generated artifacts. They all carry autogenerated headers, so prefer regenerating them from their source generator instead of hand-editing them.
- Metamodel contents are stored by name: `EPackage.eClassifiers` and `EClass.eStructuralFeatures` are dictionaries keyed by the element name. Adding another element with the same name replaces the previous entry.
- Inheritance is represented separately from features: `EClass.eSuperTypes` is a `set`, while attributes and references live in `eStructuralFeatures`.
- Attribute types follow two patterns in the tool layer: built-in EMF scalar types are stored as string literals such as `"//EString"`, while custom scalar types are represented as `EDataType` objects with `instanceClassName`.
- The current CLI workflow expects a text or Markdown file as input. Sample prompts live under `samples/` and are written as prose descriptions of the target metamodel rather than serialized model fragments.
